edits.before: 一份由全权大臣在国外谈成的条约送回朝廷，为朝士所纠，议了很久，议不出结果。作者的一种解释是：难处不在于要不要伊犁，而在于约已经签了；认账，是失地失利权在先；翻案，得有人去谈，还得有让对方重新坐下来的筹码。
edits.after: 全权大臣崇厚使俄，谈成一份条约；崇厚为朝士所纠，议了很久，议不出结果。作者的一种解释是：难处不在于要不要伊犁，而在于约已经签了；认账，是失地失利权在先；翻案，得有人去谈，还得有让对方重新坐下来的筹码。

edits.before: A treaty negotiated abroad by a plenipotentiary envoy had been sent home to the capital. It was denounced by court officials, and the debate dragged on toward no conclusion. One reading, the author's, is that the trouble was never whether Ili mattered, but that the treaty had already been signed. Accept it, and the lost territory and compromised rights stood as a fait accompli. Repudiate it, and someone had to go back to the table carrying enough leverage to make the other side sit down again.
edits.after: Chong Hou, a plenipotentiary envoy sent to Russia, concluded a treaty. Chong Hou was censured by court officials, and the debate dragged on toward no conclusion. One reading, the author's, is that the trouble was never whether Ili mattered, but that the treaty had already been signed. Accept it, and the lost territory and compromised rights stood as a fait accompli. Repudiate it, and someone had to go back to the table carrying enough leverage to make the other side sit down again.

edits.before: 僵局之中，左宗棠上奏，逐条点出哪几处不可许，主张「先之以議論，委婉而用機，次決之以戰陣，堅忍而求勝」。奏上获嘉许，他于是自请出屯哈密。六年四月，他「輿櫬發肅州」，五月抵哈密。明年正月，和议成，交还伊犁。
edits.after: 僵局之中，左宗棠上奏，逐条点出哪几处不可许，主张「先之以議論，委婉而用機，次決之以戰陣，堅忍而求勝」。奏上获嘉许，他于是自请出屯哈密。六年四月，他「輿櫬發肅州」，五月抵哈密。七月，他奉诏入都备顾问，由锦棠接替。明年正月，和议成，交还伊犁。

edits.before: Into that deadlock stepped Zuo Zongtang with a memorial. Item by item he named the terms that must not be accepted, and argued that one should "first take the matter up in negotiation, tactful and alert to opportunity, then settle it on the field of battle, patient and set on victory." The throne commended it, and he then asked leave to move his headquarters to Hami. In the fourth month of the sixth year he "set out from Suzhou with a coffin in his carriage," and reached Hami in the fifth month. In the first month of the following year, peace was concluded and Ili was returned.

In the fourth month of the sixth year he "set out from Suzhou with a coffin in his carriage," and reached Hami in the fifth month. In the seventh month he was summoned to the capital and Jintang took his place. In the first month of the following year, peace was concluded and Ili was returned.

edits.before: After the Ili crisis, the court ordered Zuo Zongtang to detach troops to garrison Suzhou, and he sent Xu Zhanbiao with six thousand men. The biography records a separate episode: when Russia was at war with Turkey, Jin Shun asked to exploit the opening and strike Ili. Zuo refused: "No. If our army does not act from a position of right, we hand them their excuse."

edits.before: The Russian side laid out three heads of demand: trade, borders, and indemnity. Chong Hou concluded the treaty on the spot, and he moved fast — the history reaches for one blunt word: "Chong Hou hastily concluded the treaty." Once the treaty existed, the court officials impeached it, and the debate went on without decision. The treaty had been signed, yet court officials denounced it and the debate stalled; the whole affair hung in mid-air.

edits.before: Zuo's memorial opened by doing the arithmetic. Since Russia occupied Ili it had been nibbling away without pause, until Xinjiang looked set to shrink by a hundred li a day. Russia treated Ili as an outer treasury: the moment we asked for the land back, it demanded five million rubles in compensation. "So Russia's return of Ili would cost Russia nothing; what we would get is only a wasteland on the outskirts." The recovery would be nominal, and the real profit would stay on the other side. The figure is recorded as the history gives it and has not been verified.

edits.before: If the Russians had wrongly presumed we were weary of war, the answer had to put both options on the table at once: "first take the matter up in negotiation, tactful and alert to opportunity, then settle it on the field of battle, patient and set on victory" — closing with "Though I am old, tired, and of no great ability, how dare I not do my best." Negotiation and battle were not alternatives to choose between; they were two steps in a fixed order.

edits.before: The author's reading is that this memorial carried weight through its structure, not merely its stance. It broke the objection into items — one for the border terms, one for trade, each with its own stated reason for refusal. It wrote the plan as a sequence: negotiation first, battle second. That the court then sent Zeng Jize to revise the earlier treaty, and that Chong Hou was punished and dismissed, is on the record. After the memorial was commended, he volunteered to hold Hami, making the second step concrete — a named man in a named place.
